messages:
support_lee: heads up — VeloxHealth (enterprise) opened a high-priority ticket: sudden p50/p95 spikes on the /v1/embeddings endpoint since ~11:28 UTC. They say it started after a bulk ingest. attaching their snippet and sample timestamps.

maria-ops: thanks, lee. can you paste the customer's request id or a sample request payload? also any customer-side throttling?

support_lee: pasted below (redacted):
```
{
  "customer_id": "velox-999",
  "requests": [ ... large batch of 2500 texts ... ],
  "model": "open-embed-medium-v1",
  "parallelism": 50
}
```
They say they used parallel uploads from 20 clients. No retries reported.

daniel: copying in @maria-ops and @tara. initial checks: 1) infra deploys in last hour? 2) routing changes? 3) autoscaler events?

sre-bot: deploy-bot reported no successful deploys in the last 2 hours to embedding clusters. autoscaler: scaled up 0 -> 2 nodes at 10:40 UTC for other customers, then down at 11:05.

maria-ops: looking at metrics — there's a clear spike in request queue length and CPU on embedding-pool-eu-west starting 11:27 UTC. p50 jumped from ~35ms -> 420ms, p95 -> 2.1s. Token throughput per worker dropped briefly.

tara: any model switch or quantization profile changes? model catalog shows same revision. but I see we promoted a new kernel selection patch yesterday to reduce memory for long-seq inferences — could be affecting batching behavior. tagging @daniel for runtime kernel context.

daniel: noted. can someone fetch the request router trace for the Velox requests? look for route decision (hosted vs dedicated) and batch sizes. command: `curl -s https://ops-api/internal/traces?req_id=velox-999&since=11:20`

maria-ops: trace results: most requests routed to hosted-embed-pool-3 (EU). batch sizes show a lot of small singleton batches interleaved with very large batches (~2k tokens each). KV cache hit rate dropped to 12% for this tenant due to many unique prefixes.

aaron: that pattern (many different small prefixes + huge batches) can cause memory pressure and suboptimal kernel selection — the runtime may oscillate between continuous-batching and single-request codepaths. also noticed GPUTemp on node03 hit 83C at 11:30.

support_lee: customer just responded: they can throttle intake if we need, but they want an internal root cause. they're worried about SLA impact.

tara: mitigation options: 1) throttle parallelism for this tenant at router level to limit inflight to 8, 2) route Velox to dedicated small pool (if available), 3) increase batch size cap so we avoid huge multi-thousand token batches, 4) rollback kernel patch if provable. which is quickest?

maria-ops: fastest is router throttling (1) — can be done in config and takes ~5min to propagate. routing to dedicated requires checking capacity; likely 20-30min to spin up.

daniel: do throttling immediately and also flip on the fallback policy to route to a compat-model (open-embed-small-v1) for requests that exceed batch size threshold. add a short-term autoscaler tweak to keep min nodes +1 while we stabilize.

maria-ops: doing router throttle now: `PATCH /internal/router/tenants/velox-999` body `{ "max_inflight": 8 }` — applying. will monitor.

sre-bot: router config change applied (11:58:03 UTC) by maria-ops.

maria-ops: monitoring dashboards — queue length dropping after ~11:59. p95 back to ~480ms and trending down. CPU on node03 falling.

aaron: good. we should still capture a full diagnostic dump (kernels, batch histograms, memmaps) for postmortem. tara, can you trigger the diagnostic snapshot for embed-pool-3? command: `curl -XPOST https://ops-api/internal/pools/embed-pool-3/diag?snapshot=true`

tara: triggered at 12:02 UTC. snapshot id: snap-2025-1752003720. uploading to /mnt/ops/snapshots/snap-2025-1752003720.tgz

daniel: next actions: - keep throttle until EOD or until we confirm kernel patch impact - run A/B test of kernel rollback in staging - evaluate router heuristics to detect large-batch anomalies - follow up with customer postmortem and mitigation notes. I'll own kernel rollback trial. @tara please own diagnostic analysis. @maria-ops keep monitoring and coordinate capacity. @support_lee follow up with Velox.

support_lee: will update customer: we applied a temporary throttle and autoscaler bump; collecting diagnostics; ETA for deeper RCA 24 hours. Velox accepted temporary throttling for now. :thumbsup:

maria-ops: logging ticket to backlog as `RTE-1439 VeloxHealth embeddings p95 spike — investigate kernel/batching interplay` and marking priority P1 for 24h window.

sre-bot: ticket RTE-1439 created by maria-ops at 12:06 UTC.

deploy-bot: scheduled canary test for kernel rollback in staging at 16:00 UTC today (no prod changes yet).

daniel: thanks all. if throttle stabilizes and snapshot shows nothing else then likely interaction of batch size + kernel heuristics. we should consider a short-term safety limiter in router to reject single huge batches or split them. add that to action items.

tara: adding notes to RTE-1439: include snapshot path, trace IDs, perf counters. will attach when analysis is complete.

support_lee: will post a short customer-facing summary once you confirm next steps.

aaron: one more note — recommend we add a telemetry alert for sudden KV-hitrate drops per-tenant, that could catch this earlier. filing small infra task now.

maria-ops: copying final ops timeline into ticket and closing this slack thread. continuing follow-ups in RTE-1439.

daniel: closing here. great fast response.
